book_title:
The Holy Gospel of Jesus Christ
according to Luke.

intros.title: THE ARGUMENT OF S. LUKES GOSPEL.
intros.text:
S. LUKES Goſpel may be diuided into fiue partes.
The firſt part is, of the Infancie both of the precurſor, and of Chriſt himſelf: chap. 1 and 2. The ſecond, of the Preparation that was made to the manifeſtation of Chriſt: chap. 3 and a piece of the 4.
The third, of Chriſtes manifeſting himſelf, by preaching and miracles, ſpecially in Galilee: the other piece of the 4. chap. vnto the middes of the 17.
The fourth of his comming into Iurie towards his Paſſion: the other piece of the 17. chap. vnto the middes of the 19.
The fifth, of the Holy Weeke of his Paſſion in Hieruſalem: the other part of the 19. chap. vnto the end of the booke.
S. Luke was ſectator (ſaith S. Hierome ) that is, a diſciple of the Apoſtle Paul, and a companion of [1] al his peregrination. And the ſame we ſee in the Actes of the Apoſtles: Where, from the 16. chap. S. Luke putteth himſelf in the traine of S. Paul, writing thus in the ſtorie. Forthwith we ſought to goe into Macedonia. And in like maner, in the firſt perſon, commonly through the reſt of that booke. Of him and his Goſpel, S. Hierom vnderſtandeth this ſaying of S. Paul: We haue ſent with him the brother, whoſe praiſe is in the Goſpel through al Churches. Where alſo he addeth: Some ſuppoſe, [2] ſo often as Paul in his Epiſtles ſaith, According to my Goſpel, that he meaneth of Lukes booke. And againe: Luke learned the Goſpel not onely of the Apoſtle Paul, who had not been with our Lord in fleſh, but of the other Apoſtles: which himſelf alſo in the beginning of his booke declareth, ſaying, As [3] they deliuered to vs who themſelves from the beginning ſaw, and were miniſters of the word. It foloweth in S. Hierome: Therfore he wrote the Goſpel, as he had heard; but the Actes of the Apoſtles he compiled as he had ſeen. S. Paul writeth of him by name to the Coloſſians : Luke the [4] Phyſicion ſaluteth you. And to Timothee : Luke alone is with me. Finally of his end thus doth S. [5] Hierome write: He liued foureſcore and foure yeres, hauing no wife. He is buried at Conſtantinople; [6] to which citie his bones with the Relikes of Andrew the Apoſtle were tranſlated out of Achaia the twentieth yere of ˹Conſtantinus˺. And of the ſame Tranſlation alſo in another place againſt [7] [8] Vigilantius the Heretike: It grieueth him that the Relikes of the Martyrs are couered with pretious couerings, and that they are not either tied in cloutes or throwen to the dunghil. Why, are we then [9] ſacrilegious, when we enter the Churches of the Apoſtles? Was ˹Conſtantinus˺ the Emperour [10] ſacrilegious, who tranſlated to Conſtantinople the holy Relikes of Andrew, Luke, and Timothee: at which the Devil's rore, and the inhabiters of Vigilantius confeſſe that they feele their preſence? His ſacred body is now at Padua in Italie, wither it was againe tranſlated from Conſtantinople.

verses.text: <sc>BECAVSE</sc> many haue gone about to compile a narration of the things that haue been accompliſhed among vs:
according as they haue deliuered vnto vs, vvho from the beginning them ſelues ſavv and vvere miniſters of the vvord:
it ſeemed good alſo vnto me hauing diligently atteined to al things from the beginning, to vvrite to thee in order, good <cr>[1]</cr> Theophilus,
that thou maiſt knovv the veritie of thoſe vvordes vvhereof thou haſt been inſtructed.

<cr>[1]</cr> There vvas in the daies of Herod the king of Ievvrie, a certaine Prieſt named Zacharie, of the <na>[2]</na> courſe of Abia: and his vvife of the daughters of Aaron, and her name Elizabeth.

notes.text: The Goſpel vpon the eue of S. Iohn Baptiſt.

verses.text: And they vvere both iuſt before God, vvalking in al the commaundements and iuſtifications of our Lord vvithout blame,
and they had no ſonne: for that Elizabeth vvas barren, and both vvere vvel ſtriken in their daies.
And it came to paſſe: vvhen he executed the prieſtly function in the order of his courſe before God,
according to the cuſtome of the Prieſtly function, he vvent forth by lot <cr>[1]</cr> to offer incenſe, entring into the temple of our Lord:
and <cr>[1]</cr> al the multitude of the people vvas <na>[2]</na> praying vvithout at the houre of the incenſe.

notes.text: We ſee here that the Prieſt did his dutie within, the people in the meane time praying without: and that the Prieſts functions did profite then, though they neither heard nor ſaw his doings.

verses.text: And there appeared to him an Angel of our Lord, ſtanding on the right hand of the altar of incenſe.
And Zacharie vvas troubled, ſeeing him: and feare fel vpon him.
But the Angel ſaid to him, Feare not Zacharie, for thy praier is heard: and thy vvife Elizabeth ſhal beare thee a ſonne, and thou ſhalt cal his name Iohn:
and thou ſhalt haue ioy and exultation, and many ſhal reioyce in his natiuitie.
for he ſhal be great before our Lord: <na>[1]</na> and vvine and ſicer he ſhal not drinke: and he ſhal be repleniſhed vvith the Holy Ghoſt euen from his mothers vvombe.

notes.text: This abſtinence foretold and preſcribed by the Angel, ſheweth that it is a worthy thing, and an acte of religion in S. Iohn, as it was in the Nazarites.

verses.text: and he ſhal <cr>[1]</cr> conuert many of the children of Iſrael to the Lord their God,

and he ſhal goe before him in the ſpirit and vertue of Elias: that he may conuert the hartes of the fathers vnto the children, and the incredulous to the vviſedom of the iuſt, to prepare vnto the Lord a perfect people. ⊢
And Zacharie ſaid to the Angel, VVhereby ſhal I knovv this? for I am old: and my vvife is vvel ſtriken in her daies.
And the Angel anſvvering ſaid to him, I am Gabriel that aſſiſt before God: and am ſent to ſpeake to thee, and to euangelize theſe things to thee.

And behold, <na>[1]</na> thou ſhalt be dumme, and ſhalt not be able to ſpeake vntil the day vvherein theſe things ſhal be done: for-becauſe thou haſt not beleeued my wordes, vvhich ſhal be fulfilled in their time.

notes.text: Zacharie puniſhed for doubting of the Angels word.

verses.text: And the people vvas expecting Zacharie: and they marueled that he made tariance in the temple.
And comming forth he could not ſpeake to them, and they knevv that he had ſeen a viſion in the temple. And he made ſignes to them, and remained dumme.
And it came to paſſe, after the daies of his office vvere expired, he departed into his houſe.
And after theſe daies Elizabeth his vvife conceiued: and hid her ſelf fiue moneths, ſaying,
For thus hath our Lord done to me in the daies vvherein he had reſpect to take avvay my reproche among men.
b <na>[1]</na> And in the ſixt moneth, the Angel Gabriel vvas ſent of God into a citie of Galilee, called Nazareth,

notes.text: The Goſpel vpon the Annunciation of our Lady, March 25. And on the weneſday of Imber weeke in Aduent. And for a Votiue Maſſe of our Lady in Aduent.

verses.text: <cr>[1]</cr> to a virgin deſpouſed to a man vvhoſe name vvas Ioſeph, of the houſe of Dauid: and the virgins name vvas <sc>MARIE</sc>,
And the Angel being entred in, ſaid vnto her, [1] HAILE ful of grace, our Lord is vvith thee: bleſſed art thou among vvomen.

notes.text: The beginning of the AVE MARIE. See the reſt v. 42.

verses.text: Vvho hauing heard, vvas troubled at his ſaying, and thought vvhat maner of ſalutation this ſhould be.
And the Angel ſaid to her, Feare not <sc>MARIE</sc>, for thou haſt found grace vvith God.
<cr>[1]</cr> Behold thou ſhalt conceiue in thy vvombe, and ſhalt beare a ſonne: and thou ſhalt call his name <sc>IESVS</sc>.
he ſhal be great, and ſhal be called the ſonne of the moſt High, and our Lord God ſhal giue him the ſeate of Dauid his father:
<cr>[1]</cr> and he ſhal reigne in the houſe of Iacob for euer, and of his kingdom there ſhal be no end.
And <sc>MARIE</sc> ſaid to the Angel, <na>[1]</na> How ſhal this be done? becauſe I knovv not man?

notes.text: She doubted not of the thing as Zacharie, but enquired of the meanes.

verses.text: And the Angel anſvvering, ſaid to her, The Holy Ghoſt ſhal come vpon thee, and the povver of the moſt High ſhal ouerſhadovv thee. And therfore alſo that vvhich of thee ſhal be borne Holy, ſhal be called the ſonne of God.
And behold Eliſabeth thy coſin, ſhe alſo hath conceiued a ſonne in her old age: and this moneth, is the ſixt to her that is called barren:
becauſe there ſhal not be impoſſible vvith God any word.
And MARIE ſaid, [1] BEHOLD the handmaid of our Lord, be it done to me according to thy word. ⊢ And the Angel departed from her.

notes.text: At this very moment when the B. Virgin gaue conſent, ſhe conceiued him perfect God and perfect man.

verses.text: <na>[1]</na> And <sc>MARIE</sc> riſing vp in thoſe daies, vvent vnto the hil countrie vvith ſpeede, into a citie of Iuda.

notes.text: The Goſpel vpon the Viſitation of our Lady, Iul, 2. And vpon the Imber friday in Aduent.

verses.text: and ſhe entred into the houſe of Zacharie, and ſaluted Eliſabeth.
And it came to paſſe: as Eliſabeth heard the ſalutation of <sc>MARIE</sc>, the <na>[1]</na> infant did leape in her vvombe. and Eliſabeth vvas repleniſhed vvith the Holy Ghoſt:

notes.text: Iohn the Baptiſt being yet in his mothers vvombe, reioyced and acknowledged the preſence of Chriſt and his mother.

verses.text: and ſhe cried out vvith a loude voice, and ſaid, BLESSED art thou among vvomen, and bleſſed is the fruite of thy vvombe.
And vvhence is this to me, that the mother of my Lord doth come to me?
For behold as the voice of thy ſalutation ſounded in mine eares, the infant in my vvombe did leape for ioy.
And bleſſed is ſhe that beleeued, becauſe thoſe things ſhal be accompliſhed that vvere ſpoken to her by our Lord.
And MARIE ſaid, [1] MY SOVLE doth magnifie our Lord.

notes.text: MAGNIFICAT at Euenſong.

verses.text: And my ſpirit hath reioyced in God my Sauiour. ⊢
Becauſe he hath regarded the humilitie of his handmaid: for behold from hence forth [1] al generations ſhal call me bleſſed.

notes.text: Haue the Proteſtants had alwaies generations to fulfil this prophecie? or do they call her bleſſed, that derogate what they can from her graces, bleſſings, and al her honour?

verses.text: Becauſe he that is mightie hath done great things to me, and holy is his name.
And his mercie from generation vnto generations, to them that feare him.
He hath ſhewed might in his arme: he hath diſperſed the proude in the conceit of their hart.
He hath depoſed the mightie from their ſeate, and hath exalted the humble.
The hungrie he hath filled vvith good things: and the riche he hath ſent away emptie.
He hath receiued Iſrael his childe, being mindeful of his mercie,
As he ſpake to our fathers, to Abraham and his ſeede for euer.
And <sc>MARIE</sc> taried with her about three moneths: and ſhe returned into her houſe.
<na>[1]</na> And Eliſabeths ful time vvas come to be deliuered: and ſhe bare a ſonne.

notes.text: The Goſpel vpon the Natiuitie of S. Iohn Baptiſt Iun. 24. called Midſommer day.

verses.text: And her neighbours and kinsfolke heard that our Lord did magnifie his mercie vvith her, and they did congratulate her.
And it came to paſſe: on the eight day they came to circumciſe the childe, and they called him by his fathers name, Zacharie.
And his mother anſvvering, ſaid, Not ſo, but he ſhal be called Iohn.
And they ſaid to her, That there is none in thy kinred that is called by this name.
And they made ſignes to his father, vvhat he vvould haue him called.
And demaunding a vvriting table, he vvrote, ſaying, <cr>[1]</cr> Iohn is his name. And they al marueled.
And forthvvith his mouth vvas opened, and his tonge, and he ſpake bleſſing God.
And feare came vpon al their neighbours: and al theſe things vvere bruited ouer al the hil-countrie of Iewrie:
and all that had heard, laid them vp in their hart, ſaying, what an one, trovv ye, ſhal this childe be? For the hand of our Lord vvas vvith him.
And Zacharie his father vvas repleniſhed vvith the Holy Ghoſt: and he prophecied, ſaying,
[1] BLESSED BE OVR LORD God of Iſrael: becauſe he hath viſited and vvrought the redemption of his people: ⊢

notes.text: BENEDICTVS at Laudes.

verses.text: And hath erected the horne of ſaluation to vs, in the houſe of Dauid his ſeruant.
As he ſpake by the mouth of his holy Prophets, that are from the beginning.
Saluation from our enemies, and from the hand of al that hate vs:
To worke mercie vvith our fathers: and to remember his holy teſtament,
[1] The othe vvhich he ſvvare to Abraham our father,
that he vvould giue to vs, That without feare being deliuered from the hand of our enemies, vve may ſerue him.
In holines and iuſtice before him, al our daies.
And thou childe, ſhalt be called the Prophet of the Higheſt: for [1] thou ſhalt goe before the face of our Lord to prepare his vvaies.
To giue knovvledge of ſaluation to his people, vnto remiſsion of their ſinnes,
Through the bovvels of the mercie of our God, in vvhich the [1] Orient, from on high, hath viſited vs,
To illuminate them that ſit in darkenes, and in the ſhadow of death: to direct our feete into the vvay of peace.
And the childe grew, and vvas ſtrengthened in ſpirit, and vvas <na>[1]</na> in the deſerts vntil the day of his manifeſtation to Iſrael.

notes.text: Marke that he was a voluntarie Eremite, and choſe to be ſolitarie from a childe, til he vvas to preach to the people, in ſo much that antiquitie counted him the firſt Eremite. Hiero. in vit. Pauli.

verses.text: <sc>AND</sc> <na>[1]</na> it came to paſſe, in thoſe daies there came forth an edict from Caeſar Auguſtus, <na>[2]</na> that the vvhole vvorld ſhould be enrolled.

notes.text: The Goſpel at the firſt Maſs vpon Chriſtmas day.

In the yere, from the creation of the world 5199: from Noës floud, 2957: from the Natiuitie of Abraham, 2015: from Moyſes and the comming forth of the people of Iſrael out of Ægypt, 1510: from Dauid anointed king, 1032: from the firſt Olympias, 800: from the building of Rome, 752: hebdomada 63, according to the prophecie of Daniel (c. 9), that is, in the yere 440 or there about: in the ſixt age of the world, when there was vniuerſal peace in al the world: the eternal God and ſonne of the eternal Father, meaning to conſecrate and ſanctifie the world with his moſt bleſſed comming, being conceiued of the Holy Ghoſt, nine moneths after his conception, IESVS CHRIST the ſonne of God is borne in Bethlehem of Iuda, in the yere of Caeſar Auguſtus 42. Vſuard. in martyrol. Decemb. 25. according to the common ancient ſupputation.

verses.text: This firſt enrolling vvas made by the Preſident of Syria Cyrinus.
And al vvent to be enrolled, euery one into his ovvne citie.
And Ioſeph alſo vvent vp from Galilee out of the citie of Nazareth into Ievvrie, to the citie of Dauid that is called Beth-lehem: for-becauſe he vvas of the houſe and familie of Dauid,
to be enrolled vvith <sc>MARIE</sc> his deſpouſed vvife that vvas vvith childe.
And it came to paſſe, vvhen they vvere there, her daies vvere fully come that ſhe ſhould be deliuered.
And ſhe brought forth her firſt begotten ſonne, and ſvvadled him in clothes, and laid him dovvne in a manger: becauſe there vvas not place for them in the inne.
And there vvere in the ſame countrie ſhepheards watching, and keeping the night vvatches ouer their flocke.
And behold, an Angel of our Lord ſtood beſide them, and the brightnes of God did ſhine round about them, and they feared vvith a great feare.
And the angel ſaid to them, Feare not: for behold I euangelize to you great ioy, that ſhal be to al the people:
becauſe this day is borne to you a <sc>SAVIOVR</sc> which is Chriſt our Lord, in the citie of Dauid.
And this ſhal be a ſigne to you, You ſhal finde the infant ſwadled in clothes: and laid in a manger.
And ſodenly there vvas vvith the Angel a multitude of the heauenly armie, praiſing God, and ſaying,
[1] Glorie in the higheſt to God: and in earth peace to men of good vvil. ⊢

notes.text: GLORIA IN EXCELSIS at Maſſe.

verses.text: b <na>[1]</na> And it came to paſſe: after the Angels departed from them into heauen, the ſhepheards ſpake one to an other: Let vs goe ouer to Bethlehem, and let vs ſee this word that is done, vvhich our Lord hath ſhevved to vs.

notes.text: The Goſpel at the ſecond maſſe vpon Chriſtmas day. And for a Votiue of our Lady from chriſtmas to Candlemas.

verses.text: And they came with ſpeede: and they found <sc>MARIE</sc> and Ioſeph, and the infant laid in the manger.
And ſeeing it, they vnderſtood of the word that had been ſpoken to them concerning this childe.
And al that heard, did maruel: and concerning thoſe things that vvere reported to them by the ſhepheards.
But <sc>MARIE</sc> kept al theſe vvordes, conferring them in her hart.
And the ſhepheards returned, glorifying and prayſing God in al things that they had heard, and ſeen, as it was ſaid to them. ⊢

c <cr>[1]</cr> And <na>[2]</na> after eight daies vvere expired, that the childe ſhould be circunciſed: his name vvas called <sc>IESVS</sc>, vvhich vvas called by the Angel, before that he vvas conceiued in the vvombe. ⊢

notes.text: c The Goſpel vpon the Circumciſion of our Lord Ian. 1.

verses.text: d <cr>[1]</cr> And after the daies vvere fully ended of her purification <na>[2]</na> according to the lavv of Moyſes, they caried him into Hieruſalem, to preſent him to our Lord (

notes.text: The Goſpel vpon the Purification of our Lady or Candlemas day. · Leu. 12, 6.

verses.text: as it is vvritten in the lavv of our Lord, [1] That euery male opening the matrice, ſhal be called holy to the Lord.)
and to giue a ſacrifice <cr>[1]</cr> according as it is written in the lavv of our Lord, a paire of turtles, or tvvo yong pigeons.
And behold, there vvas a man in Hieruſalem, named Simeon, and this man was iuſt and religious, expecting the conſolation of Iſrael: and the Holy Ghoſt vvas in him.
And he had receiued an anſwer of the Holy Ghoſt, that he ſhould not ſee death vnles he ſavv firſt the <cr>[1]</cr> <sc>CHRIST</sc> of our Lord.
And he came in ſpirit into the temple. And vvhen his parents brought in the childe <sc>IESVS</sc>, to doe according to the cuſtome of the Lavv for him:
he alſo tooke him into his armes, and bleſſed God, and ſaid,
[1] NOW THOV doeſt dimiſſe thy ſeruant O Lord, according to thy vvord in peace.

notes.text: NVNC DIMITTIS at Complin.

verses.text: Becauſe mine eies haue ſeen, thy Salvation,
Which thou hast prepared before the face of al peoples:
A light to the reuelation of the Gentils, and the glorie of thy people Iſrael. ⊢
And his father and mother vvere marueling vpon thoſe things vvhich vvere ſpoken concerning him.
And Simeon bleſſed them, and ſaid to <sc>MARIE</sc> his mother, Behold this is ſet vnto the ruine, and vnto the reſurrection of many in Iſrael, and for a ſigne vvhich ſhal be contradicted,
and <na>[1]</na> thine ovvne ſoule ſhal a ſword pearce, that out of many hartes cogitations may be reuealed.

notes.text: Simeon prophecied not only of Chriſt but of our B. Lady, of al her ſorowes: wherein ſhe was alwaies partaker with our Sauiour, from his flight into Ægypt euen to his death.

verses.text: And there vvas Anne a prophetiſſe, the daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Aſer: ſhe was farre ſtriken in daies, and had liued vvith her huſband ſeuen yeres from her virginitie.
And ſhe vvas a vvidovv vntil eightie and foure yeres: vvho departed not from the temple, by faſtings and praiers <na>[1]</na> ſeruing night and day.

notes.text: λατρέυουσα.

verses.text: And ſhe at the ſame houre ſodenly comming in, confeſſed to our Lord: and ſpake of him to al that expected the redemption of Iſrael.
And after they had vvholy done al things according to the lavv of our Lord, they returned into Galilee, into their citie Nazareth.
And the childe grevv, and vvaxed <na>[1]</na> <alt>‘ſtrong</alt>': ful of wiſedom, and the grace of God vvas in him.

notes.text: ‘ſtrong in ſpirit:

verses.text: And his parents vvent euery yere vnto Hieruſalem, <cr>[1]</cr> at the ſolemne day of Paſche.
<na>[1]</na> And when he vvas tvvelue yeres old, they going vp into Hieruſalem according to the cuſtome of the feſtiual day,

notes.text: The Goſpel vpon the firſt Sunday after the Epiphanie.

verses.text: and hauing ended the daies, vvhen they returned, the childe <sc>IESVS</sc> remained in Hieruſalem: and his parents knew it not.
And thinking that he vvas in the companie, they came a daies iourney, and ſought him among their kinſfolke and acquaintance.
And not finding him, they returned into Hieruſalem, ſeeking him.
And it came to paſſe, after three daies they found him in the temple ſitting in the middes of the Doctors, hearing them, and aſking them.
And al vvere aſtonied that heard him, vpon his vviſedom and anſvvers.
And ſeeing him, they vvondered. And his mother ſaid to him, Sonne, vvhy haſt thou ſo done to vs? behold thy father and I ſorovving did ſeeke thee.
And he ſaid to them, VVhat is it that you ſought me? did you not knovv, that I muſt be about thoſe things, vvhich are my fathers?
And they vnderſtood not the vvord that he ſpake vnto them.
And he vvent dovvne vvith them, and came to Nazareth: and vvas ſubiect to them. And his mother kept al theſe vvordes in her hart.
And <sc>IESVS</sc> proceeded in vviſedom and age, and grace vvith God and men. ⊢

chapters.summary: The Natiuitie of Chriſt, 8. and manifeſtation thereof to the Shepheards by an Angel, and by them to others. 21. His Circunciſion. 22. And <cr>[1]</cr> he came into al the countrie of Iordan, preaching the baptiſme of <na>[2]</na> penance vnto remiſſion of ſinnes: as it is vvritten in the booke of the ſayings of Eſay the Prophet:

notes.text: Penance prepareth the way to Chriſt.

verses.text: [1] A voice of one crying in the deſert: prepare the vvay of our Lord, make ſtraight his pathes.
Euery valley ſhal be filled: and euery mountaine and hil ſhal be made lovv, and crooked things ſhal become ſtraight: and rough vvaies, plaine:
and al fleſh ſhal ſee the SALVATION of God.
He ſaid therfore to the multitudes that vvent forth to be baptized of him, <cr>[1]</cr> Ye vipers broodes, vvho hath ſhewed you to flee from the vvrath to come?
Yeld therfore <na>[1]</na> fruites vvorthie of penance. and doe ye not begin to ſay, VVe haue Abraham to our father. For I tel you, that God is able of theſe ſtones to raiſe vp children to Abraham.

notes.text: Fruites of penance be workes ſatisfactorie.

verses.text: And novv the axe is put to the roote of the trees. <na>[1]</na> Euery tree therfore that yeldeth not good fruite, <na>[2]</na> <alt>‘ſhal be</alt>' cut dovvne, and caſt into fire.

notes.text: A man without good workes is vnfruitful, and ſhal be caſt into euerlaſting fire.

And he anſvvering, ſaid vnto them: <na>[1]</na> He that hath tvvo coates, let him giue to him that hath not: and he that hath meate, let him doe likevviſe.

notes.text: Almes counſeled or enioyned for ſinnes and to auoid damnation.

verses.text: And the Publicans alſo came to be baptized, and ſaid to him, Maiſter, vvhat ſhal vve doe?
But he ſaid to them, Doe nothing more then that vvhich is appointed you.
And the ſouldiars alſo aſked him, ſaying, VVhat ſhal vve alſo doe? And he ſaid to them, Vexe not neither calumniate any man: and be content vvith your ſtipends.
And <na>[1]</na> the people imagining, and al men thinking in their harts of Iohn, leſt perhaps he vvere Chriſt:

notes.text: Iohn was ſo holy that many might by errour eaſily thinke he was Chriſt.

verses.text: Iohn anſwered, ſaying vnto al, <cr>[1]</cr> I in deede baptize you vvith vvater: <cr>[2]</cr><na>[3]</na> but there <na>[4]</na> <alt>‘ſhal come</alt>' a mightier then I, vvhoſe latchet of his ſhoes I am not vvorthie to vnlooſe, he ſhal baptize you in the Holy Ghoſt and fire.

notes.text: How ſay then the Heretikes that the Baptiſme of Chriſt is of no greater vertue then Iohns?

Many other things alſo exhorting did he euangelize to the people.
<cr>[1]</cr> And Herod the Tetrarch, vvhen he vvas rebuked of him for Herodias his <na>[2]</na> <alt>‘brothers</alt>' vvife, and for al the euils vvhich Herod did:

chapters.summary: Iohn, to prepare al to Chriſt (as Eſay had prophecied of him) baptizeth them to penance; 7. inſinuating their reprobation, and the Gentils vocation, 10. teaching alſo and exhorting ech ſort to doe their dutie. 15. That him ſelf is not Chriſt, he ſheweth by the difference of their two baptiſmes: 17. and ſaith that Chriſt wil alſo iudge his baptized. 19. Iohns impriſonment. 21. Chriſt being him ſelf alſo baptized of Iohn, hath teſtimonie from heauen, 23. as he whoſe generation reduceth vs againe to God. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text: THE SECOND part: The preparation that vvas made to the manifeſtation of CHRIST.

verses.text: <sc>AND <cr>[1]</cr> IESVS</sc> ful of the Holy Ghoſt, returned from Iordan, and vvas driuen in the ſpirit into the deſert,
<na>[1]</na> fourtie daies, and vvas tempted of the deuil. And he did eate nothing in thoſe daies: and vvhen they vvere ended, he vvas an hungred.

notes.text: The Chuches faſt of 40 daies (called Lent) commeth of this, & is an Apoſtolical Tradition. Clem. Conſtit. Apoſt. li. 5 c. 13. Hier. ep. ad Marcel. adu erro. Montani. Leo ſer. 6 et 9 de Quadrages.

verses.text: And the Deuil ſaid to him, If thou be the ſonne of God, ſay to this ſtone that it be made bread.
And IESVS made anſvver vnto him, It is vvritten, [1] That not in bread alone ſhal man liue, but in euery vvord of God.
And the Deuil brought him into an high mountaine, and ſhevved him al the kingdoms of the vvhole vvorld in a moment of time:
and he ſaid to him, To thee vvil I giue this vvhole povver, and the glorie of them: for to me they are deliuered, and to vvhom I vvil, I doe giue them.
Thou therfore if thou vvilt adore before me, they ſhal al be thine.
And IESVS anſvvering ſaid to him, It is vvritten, [1][2] Thou ſhalt adore the Lord thy God, and him only ſhalt thou [3] ſerue.

notes.text: See the Annot. in S. Matthew c. 4, 11.
λατρεύσεις.

verses.text: And he brought him into Hieruſalem, and ſet him vpon the pinnacle of the temple: and he ſaid to him, If thou be the ſonne of God, caſt thy ſelf from hence downeward.
For [1] it is written, that [2] He hath giuen his Angels charge of thee, that they preſerue thee:

notes.text: If the Diuel him ſelf alleage Scripture againſt Chriſt, no maruel that Heretikes do ſo againſt Chriſts Church.

verses.text: and that in their hands they ſhal beare thee vp, leſt perhaps thou knocke thy foote againſt a ſtone.
And IESVS anſvvering ſaid to him, It is ſaid, [1] Thou ſhal not tempt the Lord thy God.
And al the tentation being ended, the Deuil departed from him vntil a time.
<cr>[1]</cr><na>[2]</na> And <sc>IESVS</sc> returned in the force of the ſpirit into Galilee, and the fame vvent forth through the vvhole countrie of him.

notes.text: THE third part: of Chriſtes manifeſting him ſelf by preaching and miracles, ſpecially in Galilee.

verses.text: And he taught in their ſynagogs, and vvas magnified of al.
<cr>[1]</cr> And he came to Nazareth vvhere he vvas brought vp: and he entred <na>[2]</na> according to his cuſtom on the Sabboth day into the ſynagogue: and he roſe vp to reade.

notes.text: Our Sauiour vſed to preach in their Synagogues.

verses.text: And the booke of Eſay the Prophet vvas deliuered vnto him. And as he vnfolded the booke, he found the place vvhere it vvas vvritten,
[1] The Spirit of the Lord vpon me, for vvhich he anointed me, to euangelize vnto the poore he ſent me, to heale the contrite of hart,
to preach to the captiues remiſsion, and ſight to the blinde, to dimiſſe the bruiſed vnto remiſſion, to preach the acceptable yere of the Lord, and the day of retribution.
And vvhen he had folded the booke, he rendred it to the miniſter, and ſate dovvne. And the eies of al in the ſynagogue vvere bent vpon him.
And he began to ſay vnto them: That this day is fulfilled this ſcripture in your eares.
And al gaue teſtimomonie to him: and they <na>[1]</na> marueled in the vvordes of grace that proceded from his mouth, and they ſaid, Is not this Ioſephs ſonne?

notes.text: He had a maruelous grace, and an extraordinarie force in mouing the harts of his hearers.

verses.text: [1] And he ſaid to them, Certes you vvil ſay to me this ſimilitude, Phyſicion, cure they ſelf: as great things as vve haue heard done in Capharnaum, doe alſo here in thy countrie.

notes.text: The Goſpel vpon Munday in the 3 vveeke of Lent.

verses.text: And he ſaid, Amen I ſay to you, that no Prophet is accepted in his ovvne countrie.

In truth I ſay to you, <cr>[1]</cr> there vvere many vvidovves in the daies of Elias in Iſrael, vvhen the heauen vvas ſhut three yeres and ſix moneths, vvhen there vvas a great famine made in the whole earth:
and to none of them vvas Elias ſent, but into Sarepta of Sidon, to a vvidovv vvoman.
<cr>[1]</cr> And there vvere many lepers in Iſrael vnder Eliſæus the Prophet: and none of them vvas made cleane but Naaman the Syrian.
And al in the ſynagogue vvere filled vvith anger, hearing theſe things.
And they roſe, and caſt him out of the citie: and they brought him to the edge of the hil, vvherevpon their citie vvas built, that they might throvv him dovvne headlong.
But he paſſing through the middes of them, vvent his vvay. ⊢
<cr>[1]</cr> And he vvent dovvne into Capharnaum a citie of Galilee: and there he taught them on the Sabboths.
And they vvere aſtonied at his doctrine: becauſe his talke vvas in povver.
And in the ſynagogue there vvas a man hauing an vncleane Diuel, and he cried out vvith a loud voice,
ſaying, Let be, vvhat to vs and thee IESVS of Nazareth? art thou come to deſtroy vs? I know thee vvho thou art, the SAINCT of God.
And <sc>IESVS</sc> rebuked him, ſaying, Hold thy peace, & goe out of him. And vvhen the Deuil had throvven him into the middes, he vvent out of him, and hurted him nothing.
And there came feare vpon al, and they talked together one vvith an other, ſaying, VVhat vvord is this, that in povver and vertue he commaundeth the vncleane ſpirits, and they goe out?
And the fame of him vvas publiſhed into euery place of the countrie.
<cr>[1]</cr> And <sc>IESVS</sc> riſing vp out of the ſynagogue, entred into Simons houſe. <na>[2]</na> And Simons vviues mother vvas holden with a great feuer: and they beſought him for her.

notes.text: The Goſpel vpon Thurſday in the 3. vveeke of Lent. And vpon Imber Saturday in Whitſunweek. And in time of mortality. See Mar. 8, 22. in margin.

verses.text: And ſtanding ouer her, he commaunded the feuer, and it left her. And incontinent riſing, ſhe miniſtred to them.
And vvhen the ſunne vvas dovvne, al that had diſeaſed of ſundrie maladies, brought them to him. But he impoſing hands vpon euery one, cured them.
And Deuils vvent out from many, crying and ſaying, That thou art the ſonne of God. And rebuking them he ſuffred them not to ſpeake, that they knevv he vvas Chriſt.
And vvhen it vvas day, going forth he vvent into a deſert place: and the multitudes ſought him, and came euen vnto him: and they held him that he ſhould not depart from them.
To vvhom he ſaid, That to other cities alſo muſt I euangelize the kingdom of God: becauſe therfore I vvas ſent.
And he vvas preaching in the ſynagogs of Galilee. ⊢

chapters.summary: Chriſt going into the Deſert to prepare him ſelf before his manifeſtation, ouercommeth the tentations of the Diuel. 14. then beginning gloriouſly in Galilee, 16. he ſheweth to them of Nazareth his commiſsion out of Eſay the Prophet, 23. inſinuating by occasion the Iewes his countrimens reprobation. 31. In Capharnaum his doctrine is admired, 33. ſpecially for his miracle in the Synagogue. 38. from which, going to Peters houſe, he ſhevveth there much more power. 42. Then retiring into the vvilderneſſe, he preacheth afterward to the other cities of Galilee.

verses.text: <sc>AND</sc> <na>[1]</na> it came to paſſe, vvhen the multitudes preſſed vpon him to heare the vvord of God, and him ſelf ſtoode beſide the lake of Geneſareth.

notes.text: The Goſpel vpon the 4 Sunday after Pentecoſt.

verses.text: <cr>[1]</cr> And he ſavv tvvo ſhippes ſtanding by the lake: and the fiſhers vvere gone dovvne, and vvaſhed their nettes.
And he going vp into one ſhip that vvas Simons, deſired him to bring it backe a litle from the land. And ſitting, he taught the multitudes out of the ſhip.
And as he ceaſed to ſpeake, he ſaid to Simon, Launche forth into the deepe, and let looſe your nettes to make a draught.
And Simon anſvvering, ſaid to him, Maiſter, labouring al the night, vve haue taken nothing: but in thy vvord I vvil let looſe the nette.
And vvhen they had done this, they incloſed a very great multitude of fiſhes, and their nette vvas broken.
And they beckened to their fellovves that vvere in the other ſhip, that they ſhould come and help them. And they came and filled both ſhippes, ſo that they did ſinke.
VVhich vvhen Simon Peter did ſee, he fel dovvne at <sc>IESVS</sc> knees, ſaying, Goe forth from me, becauſe I am a ſinful man, O Lord.
For he vvas vvholy aſtoniſhed and al that vvere vvith him, at the draught of fiſhes which they had taken.
In like maner alſo Iames and Iohn the ſonnes of Zebedee, vvho vvere Simons fellovves. And <sc>IESVS</sc> ſaid to Simon, Feare not: from this time novv, thou ſhalt be taking men.
And hauing brought their ſhippes to land, leauing al things they folovved him. ⊢

<cr>[1]</cr> And it came to paſſe, vvhen he vvas in one of the cities, and behold a man ful of leproſie, and ſeeing <sc>IESVS</sc>, and falling on his face, beſought him ſaying, Lord, if thou vvilt, thou canſt make me cleane.
And ſtretching forth the hand, he <na>[1]</na> touched him, ſaying, I vvil. be thou made cleane. And immediatly the leproſie departed from him.

notes.text: Our Saviour often healeth by touching.

verses.text: And he commaunded him that he ſhould tel no body, but, Goe, <cr>[1]</cr> ſhevv thy ſelf to the Prieſt, and offer for thy cleanſing <cr>[2]</cr> as Moyſes commaunded, for a teſtimonie to them.
But the bruite of him vvent abrode the more. and great multitudes came together to heare, and to be cured of their infirmities.
And he retired into the deſert, and praied.

<cr>[1]</cr><na>[2]</na> And it came to paſſe one day, and he ſate teaching. And there vvere Phariſees ſitting and Doctors of Lavv that vvere come out of euery tovvne of Galilee and Ievvrie and Hieruſalem: and the vertue of our Lord vvas to heale them.

notes.text: The Goſpel vpon Imber Friday in Whitſunweek.

verses.text: And behold men carying in a bed a man that had the palſey: and they ſought to bring him in, and to lay him before him.
And not finding on vvhich ſide they might bring him in for the multitude, they vvent vp vpon the roofe, and through the tiles let him dovvne vvith the bed into the middes, before <sc>IESVS</sc>.
VVhoſe faith vvhen he ſavv, he ſaid, Man, thy ſinnes are forgiuen thee.
And the Scribes and Phariſees began to thinke, ſaying, Who is this that ſpeaketh blaſphemies? Who can forgiue ſinnes, but only God?
And when <sc>IESVS</sc> knevve their cogitations, anſvvering he ſaid to them, VVhat doe you thinke in your hartes?
VVhich is eaſier to ſay, Thy ſinnes are forgiuen thee: or to ſay, Ariſe, and vvalke?
but that you may knovv that the ſonne of man hath povver in earth to forgiue ſinnes (he ſaid to the ſicke of the palſey) I ſay to thee, Ariſe, take vp thy bed, and goe into thy houſe.
And forthvvith riſing vp before them, he tooke that wherein he lay: and he vvent into his houſe, magnifying God.
And al vvere aſtonied: and they magnified God. And they vvere repleniſhed vvith feare, ſaying, That vve haue ſeen maruelous things to day. ⊢
<cr>[1]</cr><na>[2]</na> And after theſe things he vvent forth, and ſavv a Publican called Leui, ſitting at the Cuſtome-houſe, and he ſaid to him, Folovv me.

notes.text: The Goſpel vpon S. Matthew's eue. Septemb. 20.

verses.text: And leauing al things, he roſe and folovved him.
and Leui made him a great feaſt in his houſe: and there vvas a great multitude of Publicans, and of others that vvere ſitting at the table vvith them.
And their Phariſees and Scribes murmured, ſaying to his diſciples, Why doe you eate and drinke vvith Publicans and ſinners?
And <sc>IESVS</sc> anſwering ſaid to them, They that are vvhole, neede not the Phyſicion: but they that are il at eaſe.
<na>[1]</na> I came not to call the iuſt, but ſinners to penance. ⊢

notes.text: Chriſt came not to call thoſe, who preſume of their owne iuſtice, and that coumpt them ſelues to haue no neede of Chriſt.

verses.text: But they ſaid to him, <cr>[1]</cr> VVhy doe the diſciples of Iohn <cr>[2]</cr> faſt often, and make obſecrations, and of the Phariſees in like maner: but thine doe eate and drinke?
To vvhom he ſaid, Why, can you make the children of the bridegrome faſt vvhiles the bridegrome is vvith them?
But the daies vvil come: and vvhen the bridegrome ſhal be taken avvay from them, then they ſhal faſt in thoſe daies.

And he ſaid a ſimilitude alſo vnto them, That no man putteth a peece from a nevv garment into an old garment: othervviſe both he breaketh the nevv, and the peece from the nevv agreeth not vvith the old.
And no bodie putteth nevv vvine into old bottels: othervviſe the nevv vvine vvil breake the bottels, and it ſelf vvil be ſhed, and the bottels vvil be loſt.
But nevv vvine is to be put into nevv bottels: and both are preſerued together.
And no man drinking old, vvil nevv by and by. for he ſaith, The old is better.

chapters.summary: Hauing taught the people out of Peters ſhip, 4. he ſheweth in a miraculous taking of fiſhes, how he wil make him the fiſher of men. 12. He cureth a leper by touching him, and ſendeth him to the Prieſt in witneſſe that he is not againſt Moyſes. 15. The people flocking vnto him, he retireth into the vvilderneſſe. 17. To the Phariſees in a ſolemne aſſembly he proueth by a miracle his power to remit ſinnes in earth. 27. He defendeth his eating vvith ſinners, as being the Phyſicion of ſoules, 33. and his not preſcribing as yet of any faſtes to his Diſciples.

verses.text: <sc>AND</sc> <cr>[1]</cr> it came to paſſe on the <na>[2]</na> Sabboth ſecond-firſt, vvhen he paſſed through the corne, his Diſciples did plucke the eares, and did eate rubbing them vvith their hands.

notes.text: S. Hierom (ep. 2 ad Nepotian.) writeth of him ſelf, that being at Conſtantinople, he aſked his maiſter Gregorie Nazianzene, the famous Doctor, then Biſhop there, what Sabboth this was. who by his anſwer declared that it was very hard to tel, neither is it yet knowen to the beſt learned. Yet the Proteſtants are wont to ſay, Al is very eaſie.

verses.text: And certaine of the Phariſees ſaid to them, VVhy doe you that vvhich is not lawful on the Sabboths?
And <sc>IESVS</sc> anſvvering them, ſaid, Neither this haue you read vvhich Dauid did, vvhen him ſelf vvas an hungred and they that vvere vvith him:

<cr>[1]</cr> hovv he entred into the houſe of God, and tooke the loaues of Propoſition, and did eate, and gaue to them that vvere vvith him, vvhich it is not lavvful to eate <cr>[2]</cr> but only for Prieſts?
And he ſaid to them, That the ſonne of man is Lord of the Sabboth alſo.
And it came to paſſe on an other Sabboth alſo, that he entred into the ſynagogue, and taught. <cr>[1]</cr> And there vvas a man, and his right hand vvas vvithered.
And the Scribes and Phariſees vvatched if he vvould cure on the Sabboth: that they might finde hovv to accuſe him.
But he knevv their cogitations: and he ſaid to the man that had the withered hand, Ariſe, and ſtand forth into the middes. And riſing he ſtoode.
And <sc>IESVS</sc> ſaid to them, I aſke you, if it be lavvful on the Sabboths to doe vvel or il: to ſaue a ſoule or to deſtroy?
And looking about vpon them al, he ſaid to the man, Stretch forth thy hand. And he ſtretched it forth: and his hand vvas reſtored.
And they vvere repleniſhed vvith madnes: and they communed one with an other what they might doe to <sc>IESVS</sc>.
<na>[1]</na> And it came to paſſe in thoſe daies, he vvent forth into the mountaine to pray, and he paſſed the vvhole night in the prayer of God.

notes.text: The Goſpel vpon S. Bartholomew's day. Aug. 24.

verses.text: [1] And vvhen day vvas come, he called his Diſciples: and he choſe tvvelue of them ( vvhom alſo he named Apoſtles)
Simon vvhom he ſurnamed Peter, and Andrevv his brother, Iames and Iohn, Philippe and Bartholomew,
Matthevv and Thomas, Iames of Alphæus and Simon that is called Zelótes,
and Iude of Iames, and Iudas Iſcariote vvhich vvas the traitour.

<na>[1]</na> And deſcending vvith them he ſtoode in a plaine place, and the multitude of his Diſciples, and a very great companie of people from al Ievvrie and Hieruſalem: and the ſea coaſt both of Tyre and Sidon,

notes.text: The Goſpel vpon SS. Fabian and Sebaſtian's day, Ian. 20. upon S. Dionyſe day. Octo. 9. upon Allhallows' eue. And for many Martyrs.

verses.text: vvhich vvere come to heare him, and to be healed of their maladies. And they that vvere vexed of vncleane ſpirits, vvere cured.
And al the multitude <cr>[1]</cr> ſought to touch him, becauſe vertue vvent forth from him, and healed al. ⊢
And he lifting vp his eies vpon his Diſciples, ſaid, <cr>[1]</cr> Bleſſed are ye poore: for yours is the kingdom of God.
Bleſſed are you that novv are an hungred: becauſe you ſhal be filled. Bleſſed are you that novv doe vveepe: becauſe you ſhal laugh.
Bleſſed ſhal you be vvhen men ſhal hate you, and vvhen they ſhal ſeparate you, and vpbraide you, and abandon your name as euil, for the ſonne of mans ſake.
Be glad in that day and reioyce: for behold, your revvard is much in heauen. ⊢ for according to theſe things did their fathers to the Prophets.
But wo to you that are riche, becauſe you haue your conſolation.
VVo to you that are filled: becauſe you ſhal be hungrie. VVo to you that novv doe laugh: becauſe you ſhal mourne and vveepe.
VVo, vvhen al men ſhal bleſſe you. for according to theſe things did their fathers to the falſe-Prophets.
But to you I ſay that doe heare, Loue your enemies, doe good to them that hate you.
Bleſſe them that curſe you, and pray for them that calumniate you.
And he that ſtriketh thee on the cheeke, offer alſo the other. And from him that taketh avvay from thee thy robe, prohibit not thy coate alſo.
And <na>[1]</na> to euery one that aſketh thee, giue: and of him that taketh avvay the things that are thine, aſke not againe.

notes.text: That is, to euery one iuſtly aſking. For that which is vniuſtly aſked, may be iuſtly denied. Aug. li. 1. c. 40. de Serm. Do. in monte.

verses.text: And according as you vvil that men doe to you, doe you alſo to them in like maner.
And if you loue them that loue you, vvhat thanke is to you? for ſinners alſo loue thoſe that loue them.
And if ye doe good to them that doe you good: vvhat thanke is to you? for ſinners alſo doe this.
And if ye lend to them of vvhom ye hope to receiue: vvhat thanke is to you? for ſinners alſo lend vnto ſinners, for to receiue as much.

But loue ye your enemies: doe good and lend, hoping for nothing thereby, and your reward ſhal be much, and you ſhal be the ſonnes of the Higheſt, becauſe him ſelf is beneficial vpon the vnkinde and the euil.
<na>[1]</na> Be ye therfore merciful as alſo your father is merciful.

notes.text: The Goſpel vpon the firſt Sunday after Pentecoſt.

verses.text: Iudge not, & you ſhal not be iudged. condemne not, & you ſhal not be condemned. forgiue, and you ſhal be forgiuen.

Giue, and there ſhal be giuen to you. good meaſure & preſſed dovvne and ſhaken together and running ouer ſhal they giue into your boſome. For vvith the ſame meaſure that you do meate, it ſhal be meaſured to you againe.
And he ſaid to them a ſimilitude alſo: Can the blinde leade the blinde? doe not both fal into the ditch?
The diſciple is not aboue his maiſter: but euery one ſhal be perfect, if he be as his maiſter.
And vvhy ſeeſt thou the mote in thy brothers eie: but the beame that is in thine ovvne eie thou conſidereſt not?

Or hovv canſt thou ſay to thy brother, Brother, let me caſt out the mote out of thine eie: thy ſelf not ſeeing the beame in thine ovvne eie? Hypocrite, caſt firſt the beame out of thine ovvne eie: and then ſhalt thou ſee clerely to take forth the mote out of thy brothers eie. ⊢
For there is no good tree that yeldeth euil fruites: nor euil tree, that yeldeth good fruite.
For euery tree is knovven by his fruite. For neither doe they gather figges of thornes: neither of a buſh doe they gather the grape.
The good man of the good treaſure of his hart bringeth forth good: and the euil man of the il treaſure bringeth forth euil. for of the aboundance of the hart the mouth ſpeaketh.
And vvhy cal you me, Lord, Lord: and doe not the things vvhich I ſay?
Euery one that commeth to me, and heareth my vvords, and doeth them: I vvil ſhevv you to vvhom he is like.

He is like to a man <na>[1]</na> building a houſe, that digged deepe, and laid the foundation vpon a rocke. And vvhen an inundation roſe, the riuer bette againſt that houſe, and it could not moue it: for it vvas founded vpon a rocke.

notes.text: He buildeth right & ſurely, that hath both faith and good workes: he buildeth on ſand, that truſteth to his faith or reading or knowledge of the ſcripture, and doth not worke or liue accordingly.

verses.text: But he that heareth, and doeth not: is like to a man building his houſe vpon the earth vvithout a foundation: againſt the vvhich the riuer did beate: and incontinent it fell, and the ruine of that houſe vvas great.

chapters.summary: For reprouing by Scripture and miracle (as alſo by reaſon) the Phariſees blindnes about the obſeruation of the Sabboth, 11. they ſeeke his death. 12. Hauing in the mountaine prayed al night, he chooſeth twelue Apoſtles. 17. and after many miracles vpon the diſeaſed, 20. he maketh a ſermon to his Diſciples before the people: propoſing heauen to ſuch as wil ſuffer for him, 24. and wo to ſuch as wil not. 27. Yet vvithal exhorting to doe good euen to our enemies alſo. 19. and that the Maiſters muſt firſt mend them ſelues. 46. finally, to doe good vvorkes, becauſe only faith vvil not ſuffice.

verses.text: <sc>AND</sc> <cr>[1]</cr> vvhen he had fully ſaid al his vvords into the eares of the people, he entred into Capharnaum.
And the ſeruant of a certaine Centurion being ſicke, vvas readie to die: vvho vvas deere vnto him.
And when he had heard of <sc>IESVS</sc>, he ſent vnto him the Auncients of the Ievves, deſiring him to come and heale his ſeruant.
But they being come to <sc>IESVS</sc>, beſought him earneſtly, ſaying to him, That he is vvorthie that thou ſhouldeſt doe this for him.
for he loueth our nation: and he hath built a ſynagogue for vs.

And IESVS went with them. And vvhen he vvas novv not farre from the houſe, the Centurion ſent his frends vnto him, ſaying, Lord, trouble not thy ſelf. for [1] I am not vvorthie that thou ſhouldeſt enter vnder my roofe.

notes.text: See the Annotations vpon S. Matth. c. 8, 8.

verses.text: for the vvhich cauſe neither did I thinke my ſelf vvorthie to come to thee: but ſay the vvord, and my ſeruant ſhal be made whole.
for I alſo am a man ſubiect to authoritie, hauing vnder me ſouldiars: and I ſay to this, goe, and he goeth: and to an other, come, and he commeth: and to my ſeruant, doe this, and he doeth it.
Which <sc>IESVS</sc> hearing, marueiled: and turning to the multitudes that folovved him he ſaid, Amen I ſay to you, neither in Iſrael haue I found ſo great faith.
And they that vvere ſent, being returned home, found the ſeruant that had been ſicke, vvhole.
<na>[1]</na> And it came to paſſe, aftervvard he vvent into a citie that is called Naim: and there vvent vvith him his Diſciples and a very great multitude.

notes.text: The Goſpel vpon the 15 Sunday after Pentecoſt. And vpon Thurſday in the 4 weeke of Lent. And for S. Monica S. Auguſtins mother Maij. 4.

verses.text: And vvhen he came nigh to the gate of the citie, behold a dead man vvas caried forth, the only ſonne of his mother: and ſhe, vvas a vvidovv: and a great multitude of the citie vvith her.
Vvhom vvhen our Lord had ſeen, being moued vvith mercie vpon her, he ſaid to her, VVeepe not.
And he came neere and touched the coffin. And they that caried it, ſtood ſtil: and he ſaid, Yong man, I ſay to thee, Ariſe.
And he that vvas dead, ſate vp, and beganne to ſpeake. And he gaue him to his mother.
And feare tooke them al: and they magnified God, ſaying, That a great Prophet is riſen among vs: and, That God hath viſited his people.
And this ſaying vvent forth into al Ievvrie of him, and into al the countrie about.
And Iohns diſciples ſhevved him of al theſe things.
<cr>[1]</cr> And Iohn called tvvo of his diſciples, and ſent them to <sc>IESVS</sc>, ſaying, Art thou he that art to come: or expect vve an other?
And vvhen the men vvere come vnto him, they ſaid, Iohn the Baptiſt hath ſent vs to thee, ſaying, Art thou he that art to come: or expect vve an other?
(And the ſelf ſame houre, he cured many of maladies, and hurtes, and euil ſpirits: and to many blinde he <na>[1]</na> gaue ſight.)

notes.text: c ἐχαρίσατο.

verses.text: And anſwering, he ſaid to them, Goe and report to Iohn vvhat you haue heard and ſeen: <cr>[1]</cr> That the blinde ſee, the lame vvalke, the lepers are made cleane, the deafe heare, the dead riſe againe,
<na>[1]</na> the poore are euangelized: and bleſſed is he vvhoſoeuer ſhal not be ſcandalized in me.

notes.text: Pauperes euangelizantur, that is, to the poore the Goſpel is preached, and they receiue it.

verses.text: <cr>[1]</cr> And vvhen Iohns meſſengers vvere departed, he began to ſay of Iohn to the multitudes, VVhat vvent you out into the deſert to ſee? a reede moued vvith the vvinde?
But vvhat vvent you forth to ſee? a man clothed in <na>[1]</na> ſoft garments? behold they that are in coſtly apparel and delicacies, are in the houſe of kings.

notes.text: Marke this vvel concerning Iohns apparel and diet. See the Annotations vpon S. Matth. c. 3, 4.

verses.text: But what vvent you out for to ſee? a Prophet? Certes I ſay to you, and more then a Prophet.
this is he of vvhom it is vvritten, [1] Behold I ſend mine Angel before thy face, vvhich ſhal prepare thy vvay before thee.
For I ſay to you, A greater Prophet among the children of vvomen then Iohn the Baptiſt, there is no man. but he that is the leſſer in the kingdom of God, is greater then he.
And al the people hearing and the Publicans, iuſtified God, being baptized vvith Iohns baptiſme.
But the Phariſees and the lavvyers <na>[1]</na> deſpiſed the counſel of God againſt them ſelues, being not baptized of him.

notes.text: As they that contēned Iohns baptiſme, deſpiſed Gods counſel and wiſedō: ſo much more they that make no accoumpt of the Sacraments of the Church, deſpiſe Gods counſel and ordinance touching their ſaluation, to their owne damnation.

verses.text: And our Lord ſaid, VVherevnto then ſhal I liken the men of this generation, and vvherevnto are they like?
They are like to children ſitting in the market-place, and ſpeaking one to an other, and ſaying, VVe haue piped to you, and you haue not daunced: vve haue lamented, and you haue not vvept.
For Iohn the Baptiſt came <cr>[1]</cr> neither eating bread nor drinking vvine: and you ſay, He hath a deuil.
The ſonne of man came eating and drinking: and you ſay, Behold a man that is a gurmander and a drinker of vvine, a frende of Publicans and ſinners.
And vviſedom is iuſtified of al her children.
<na>[1]</na> And one of the Phariſees deſired him to eate vvith him. And being entred into the houſe of the Phariſee, he ſate downe to meate.

notes.text: The Goſpel vpon S. Marie Magdalens day Iul. 22. And vpon Thurſday in Paſſion weeke. And vpon Imber Friday in Sept.

verses.text: And behold a vvoman that was in the citie, a ſinner, as ſhe knevv that he vvas ſet downe in the Phariſees houſe, ſhe brought an alabaſter boxe of ointment:
and ſtanding behind beſide his feete, ſhe began to <na>[1]</na> vvater his feete vvith teares, & vviped them vvith the heares of her head, and kiſſed his feete, & anointed them with the ointment.

notes.text: A perfect paterne of true penance in this vvoman, who ſought of Chriſt with open teares & other ſtrange workes of ſatisfaction and deuotion, remiſſion of her ſinnes.

verses.text: And the Phariſee that had bid him, ſeeing it, ſpake vvithin him ſelf, ſaying, This man if he vvere a Prophet, vvould know certes vvho and vvhat maner of woman ſhe is vvhich toucheth him, that ſhe is a ſinner.
And <sc>IESVS</sc> anſwering ſaid to him, Simon, I haue ſomevvhat to ſay vnto thee. but he ſaid, Maiſter, ſay.
A certaine creditour had tvvo debters: one did ovve fiue hundred pence, and the other fiftie.
They hauing not vvherevvith to pay, he forgaue both. VVhether therfore doth loue him more?
Simon anſvvering ſaid, I ſuppoſe that he to vvhom he forgaue more. But he ſaid to him, Thou haſt iudged rightly.

And turning to the vvoman, he ſaid vnto Simon, Doeſt thou ſee this vvoman? I entred into thy houſe, vvater to my feete thou didſt not giue: but ſhe vvith teares hath vvatered my feete, and vvith her heares hath vviped them.
Kiſſe thou gaueſt me not: but ſhe ſince I came in, hath not ceaſed to kiſſe my feete.
VVith oile thou didſt not anoint my head: but ſhe vvith ointment hath anointed my feete.
For the vvhich I ſay to thee, Many ſinnes are forgiuen her, becauſe ſhe hath <na>[1]</na> loued much. But to vvhom leſſe is forgiuen, he loueth leſſe.

notes.text: Not only faith (as you may perceiue) but loue or charitie obtaineth remiſſion of ſinnes.

verses.text: And he ſaid to her, Thy ſinnes are forgiuen thee.
And they that ſate together at the table, began to ſay within them ſelues, <na>[1]</na> Who is this that alſo forgiueth ſinnes?

notes.text: As the Phariſees did alwaies carpe Chriſt for remiſſion of ſinnes in earth, ſo the Heretikes reprehend his Church that remitteth ſinnes by his authoritie.

verses.text: And he ſaid to the woman, Thy faith hath made the ſafe, goe in peace. ⊢

chapters.summary: He teſtifieth, the faith of the Centurion who was a Gentil, to be greater then he found among al the Iewes, and cureth his ſeruant abſent. 11. the vvidovves ſonne he reuiueth and reſtoreth to her, and is renowmed therevpon. 18. To Iohns meſſengers he anſwereth with miracles, leauing to Iohn to preach thereby vnto them that he is Chriſt. 24. And afterward he declareth how vvorthy credit was Iohns teſtimonie, 29. inueighing againſt the Phariſees, 31. who vvith neither of their maners of liuing could be wonne. 36. ſhewing alſo vnto them by occaſion of Marie Magdalen, how he is a frende to ſinners, not to maintaine them in ſinne, but to forgiue them their ſinnes vpon their faith and penance.

verses.text: <sc>AND</sc> it came to paſſe afterward, and he made his iourney by cities and tovvnes preaching and euangelizing the kingdom of God: and the Tvvelue vvith him,
and ſome vvomen that had been cured of wicked ſpirits and infirmities, <cr>[1]</cr> Marie vvhich is called Magdalene, out of whom ſeuen deuils vvere gone forth,
and Ioane the vvife of Chuſa Herods procurator, and Suſan, and <na>[1]</na> many others that did miniſter vnto him of their ſubſtance.

notes.text: aliæ multæ

verses.text: <cr>[1]</cr> And <na>[2]</na> vvhen a very great multitude aſſembled, and haſtened out of the cities vnto him, he ſaid by a ſimilitude.

notes.text: The Goſpel vpon the Sunday of Sexageſme.

verses.text: The ſovver vvent forth to ſovv his ſeede. and vvhiles he ſoweth, ſome fel by the vvay ſide, and vvas troden vpon, and the foules of the aire did eate it.
And other ſome fel vpon the rocke: and being ſhot vp, it withered, becauſe it had not moiſture.
And otherſome fel among thornes, and the thornes grovving vp vvithal, choked it.
And other ſome fel vpon good ground: and being ſhot vp, yelded fruite an hundred fold. Saying theſe things he cried, He that hath eares to heare, let him heare.
And his diſciples aſked him vvhat this parable was.
To vvhom he ſaid, To you it is giuen to knovv the myſterie of the kingdom of God, but to the reſt in parables, <cr>[1]</cr> that <na>[2]</na> ſeeing they may not ſee, and hearing may not vnderſtand.

notes.text: See the Annotations vpon S. Matthew. c. 13, 14.

verses.text: And the parable is this: The ſeede, is the vvord of God.
And they beſides the vvay: are thoſe that heare, then the deuil commeth, and taketh the vvord out of their hart, leſt beleeuing they be ſaued.
For they vpon the rocke: ſuch as vvhen they heare, vvith ioy receiue the vvord: and theſe haue no rootes: becauſe <na>[1]</na> for a time they beleeue, and in time of tentation they reuolt.

notes.text: Againſt the Heretikes that ſay, faith once had can not be loſt, and that he which now hath not faith, neuer had.

verses.text: And that vvhich fel into thornes, are they that haue heard, and going their vvaies, are choked vvith cares and riches and pleaſures of this life, and render not fruite.
And that vpon good ground: are they vvhich in a good and very good hart, hearing the vvord, doe reteine it, and yeld fruite in patience. ⊢
And no man lighting a candel doth couer it vvith a veſſel, or put it vnder a bed: but ſetteth it vpon a candelſticke, that they that enter in, may ſee the light.
For there is not any thing ſecrete, that ſhal not be made manifeſt: nor hid, that ſhal not be knowen, & come abrode.
See therfore how you heare. For he that hath, to him ſhal be giuen: and vvhoſoeuer hath not, that alſo vvhich he thinketh he hath, ſhal be taken avvay from him.
And <cr>[1]</cr> his mother and brethren came vnto him: and they could not come at him for the multitude.
And it vvas told him, Thy mother and thy brethren ſtand vvithout, deſirous to ſee thee.
Who anſvvering ſaid to them, My <na>[1]</na> mother and my brethren, are they that heare the vvord of God and doe it.

notes.text: He did not here diſdainfully ſpeake of his mother, but teacheth that our ſpiritual kinred is to be preferred before carnal cognation. Hilar. in 12 Mat.

verses.text: <cr>[1]</cr> And it came to paſſe one day: and he vvent vp into a boate, and his diſciples, and he ſaid to them, Let vs ſtrike ouer the lake. And they launched forth.
And vvhen they vvere ſailing, he ſlept: and there fel a ſtorme of vvinde into the lake, and they <na>[1]</na> vvere filled, and vvere in danger.

notes.text: c complebantur.

verses.text: And <na>[1]</na> they came and raiſed him, ſaying, Maiſter, vve periſh. But he riſing, rebuked the vvinde and the tempeſt of vvater: and it ceaſed, and there vvas made a calme.

notes.text: See the Annotations vpon S. Matthew c. 8, 24.

verses.text: And he ſaid to them, VVhere is your faith? Who fearing, marueiled one to an other, ſaying, VVho is this (trovv ye) that he commaundeth both the vvindes and the ſea, and they obey him?
<cr>[1]</cr> And they ſailed to the countrie of the Geraſens vvhich is ouer againſt Galilee.
And vvhen he vvas come forth to the land, there mette him a certaine man that had a deuil novv a very long time, and he did vveare no clothes, neither did he tarie in houſe, but in the monuments.
And as he ſaw <sc>IESVS</sc>, he fel dovvne before him: and crying out vvith a great voice, he ſaid, VVhat is to me and thee <sc>IESVS</sc> ſonne of God moſt high? I beſeech thee doe not torment me.

For he commaunded the vncleane ſpirit to goe forth out of the man. For many times he caught him, and he was bound vvith chaines, and kept vvith fetters: and breaking the bondes vvas driuen of the deuil into the deſerts.
And <sc>IESVS</sc> aſked him ſaying, VVhat is thy name? But he ſaid, Legion. becauſe many deuils vvere entred into him.
And they beſought him that he vvould not commaund them to goe into the depth.
And there vvas there a heard of many ſvvine feeding on the mountaine: and they deſired him, that he vvould permit them to enter into them. And he permitted them.
The deuils therfore vvent forth out of the man, and entred into the ſwine: and the heard vvith violence vvent headlong into the lake, and vvas ſtifled.
Which vvhen the ſvvineheards ſavv done, they fled: and told into the citie and into the tovvnes.

And they vvent forth to ſee that vvhich vvas done: and they came to <sc>IESVS</sc>, and found the man, out of whom the deuils vvere gone forth, ſitting at his feete, clothed, and vvel in his vvittes, and they vvere afraid.
And they alſo that had ſeen, told them hovv he had been made whole from the legion.
And al the multitude of the countrie of the Geraſens beſought him to depart from them: for they vvere taken vvith great feare. And he going vp into the boate, returned.
And the man out of vvhom the deuils vvere departed, deſired him that he might be vvith him. But <sc>IESVS</sc> dimiſſed him, ſaying,
Returne into thy houſe, and tel hovv great things God hath done to thee. And he vvent through the vvhole citie, preaching hovv great things <sc>IESVS</sc> had done to him.
And it came to paſſe: vvhen <sc>IESVS</sc> vvas returned, the multitude receiued him. and al vvere expecting him.
And <cr>[1]</cr> behold there came a man vvhoſe name vvas Iairus, and he vvas Prince of the Synagogue: and he fel at the feete of <sc>IESVS</sc>, deſiring him that he vvould enter into his houſe,
becauſe he had an only daughter almoſt tvvelue yeres old, and ſhe vvas a dying. And it chaunced, vvhiles he vvent, he vvas thronged of the multitudes.
And there vvas <na>[1]</na> a certaine vvoman in a fluxe of bloud from tvvelue yeres paſt, vvhich had beſtovved al her ſubſtance vpon Phyſicions, neither could ſhe be cured of any:

notes.text: See the Annotations vpon S. Matthew c. 9, 19.

verses.text: ſhe came behind him, and touched the hemme of his garment: and forthvvith the fluxe of her bloud ſtinted,

And <sc>IESVS</sc> ſaid, VVho is it that touched me? And al denying, <na>[1]</na> Peter ſaid, and they that vvere vvith him, Maiſter, the multitudes throng and preſſe thee, and doeſt thou ſay, VVho touched me?

notes.text: It is an euident ſigne of prerogatiue, that Peter only is named ſo often as cheefe of the company. Mar. 1, 36. Act. 5, 29. Luc. 9, 32. Mar. 16, 7. 1 Cor. 15, 5.

verses.text: And <sc>IESVS</sc> ſaid, Some bodie hath touched me. for I know that there is vertue proceded from me.

And the vvoman ſeeing, that ſhe vvas not hid, came trembling, and fel dovvne before his feete: and for vvhat cauſe ſhe had touched him, ſhe ſhevved before al the people: and hovv forthvvith ſhe vvas made vvhole.
But he ſaid to her, Daughter, thy faith hath made the ſafe, goe thy vvay in peace.
As he vvas yet ſpeaking, there commeth one to the Prince of the ſynagogue, ſaying to him, That thy daughter is dead, trouble him not.
And <sc>IESVS</sc> hearing this vvord, anſvvered the father of the maide, Feare not: <na>[1]</na> beleeue only, and ſhe ſhal be ſafe.

notes.text: See the Annotations vpon S. Marke c. 5, 36.

verses.text: And vvhen he vvas come to the houſe, he permitted not any man to enter in vvith him, but Peter, and Iames, and Iohn, and the father and mother of the maide.
And al vvept, and mourned for her. But he ſaid, VVeepe not, the maide is not dead, but ſleepeth.
And they derided him, knovving that ſhe vvas dead.
But he holding her hand cried ſaying, Maide ariſe.
And her ſpirit returned, and ſhe roſe incontinent. And he bade them giue her to eate.
And her parentes were aſtonied, whom he commaunded to tel no man that which was done.

chapters.summary: Going ouer al Galilee with his traine, 4. he preacheth to the Iewes in parables becauſe of their reprobation: 9. but to his Diſciples manifeſtly: becauſe he wil not for the Iewes incredulity haue his comming fruſtrate: 19. ſignifying alſo that we are his kinne (though we be Gentils) and not his carnal brethren the Iewes. 22. To whom alſo (ſignified by the Geraſens) after the tempeſt in his ſleepe (that is, in his death) and caulme in his reſurrection, he commeth: but they preferring their temporals before his preſence, he leaueth them againe. 41. Likewiſe comming to cure the Iewes (who were borne when the Gentils ſickened, about Abrahams time) he is preuented with the faith of the Gentils, and then the Iewes die. but them alſo in the end he wil reſtore.

verses.text: <sc>AND</sc> <cr>[1]</cr><na>[2]</na> calling together the tvvelue Apoſtles, he gaue them <na>[3]</na> vertue and povver ouer al deuils, and to cure maladies.

notes.text: The Goſpel vpon Thurſday in whitſonweeke.
To commaund Diuels and diſeaſes either of body or ſoule, is by nature proper to God onely: but by Gods gift, men alſo may haue the ſame. euen ſo to forgiue ſinnes.

verses.text: And he ſent them to preach the kingdom of God: and to heale the ſicke.
And he ſaid to them, Take nothing for the vvay, neither rod, nor ſkrippe, nor bread, nor money, neither haue tvvo coates.
And into vvhatſoeuer houſe you enter, tarie there, and thence doe not depart.
And whoſoever ſhal not receiue you, going forth out of that citie, ſhake of the duſt alſo of your feete <na>[1]</na> for a teſtimonie vpon them.

notes.text: A great fault to reiect the true preachers, or not to admit them into houſe for needful harbour and ſuſtenance.

verses.text: And going forth they vvent a circuite from tovvne to tovvne euangelizing and curing euery vvhere. ⊢
And <cr>[1]</cr> Herod the Tetrarch heard al things that vvere done by him: and he ſtaggered becauſe it vvas ſaid of ſome, That Iohn vvas riſen from the dead.
but of other ſome, That Elias hath appeared: and of others, that a Prophet one of the old ones vvas riſen.
And Herod ſaid, Iohn I haue beheaded: but vvho is this of vvhom I heare ſuch things? And he ſought for to ſee him.
And <cr>[1]</cr> the Apoſtles being returned, reported to him vvhatſoeuer they did: and taking them he retired apart into a deſert place, vvhich belongeth to Beth-ſaida.
Which the multitudes vnderſtanding, folovved him: & he receiued them, and ſpake to them of the kingdom of God, and them that had neede of cure he healed.

And the day began to dravv towards an end. And the Tvvelue comming neere, ſaid to him, Dimiſſe the multitudes, that going into tovvnes and villages here about, they may haue lodging, and finde meates: becauſe here we are in a deſert place.
And he ſaid to them, Giue you them to eate. But they ſaid, We haue no more but fiue loaues and tvvo fiſhes: vnles perhaps vve ſhould goe and bie meates for al this multitude.
And there vvere men almoſt fiue thouſand. And he ſaid to his diſciples, Make them ſit dovvne by companies fiftie and fiftie.
And ſo they did. And they made al ſit downe.
And taking the fiue loaues and the tvvo fiſhes, he looked vp vnto heauen, and <na>[1]</na><na>[2]</na> bleſſed them: and he brake, and diſtributed to his diſciples, for to ſet before the multitudes.

notes.text: c εὐλόγησεν αὐτοὺς:
Here you ſee that he bleſſed the things, and not only gaue thanks to God. See Annot. Marci. c. 8, 7.

verses.text: And <na>[1]</na> they did al eate, and had their fill. And there vvas taken vp that vvhich remained to them, tvvelue baſkets of fragments.

notes.text: The miraculous prouidence. of God toward ſuch as folow Chriſt into deſerts, priſons, baniſhment, or whitherſoeuer.

verses.text: <cr>[1]</cr> And it came to paſſe: vvhen he vvas alone praying, his diſciples alſo vvere vvith him: and he aſked them ſaying, VVhom doe the multitudes ſay that I am?
But they anſwered, and ſaid, Iohn the Baptiſt: and ſome, Elias: but ſome, that one of the Prophets before time, is riſen.
And he ſaid to them, But vvhom ſay ye that I am? Simon Peter anſvvering, ſaid, The <sc>CHRIST</sc> of God.
But he rebuking them, commaunded that they ſhould tell this to no man,
ſaying, That the ſonne of man muſt ſuffer many things, and be reiected of the Auncients and cheefe Prieſts and Scribes, and be killed, and the third day riſe againe.
And he ſaid to al, If any man vvil come after me, let him denie him ſelf, and take vp his croſſe daily, and folovv me.
For he that vvil ſaue his life, ſhal loſe it: for he that ſhal loſe his life for my ſake, ſhal ſaue it.
for vvhat profit hath a man if he gaine the vvhole vvorld, and loſe him ſelf, and caſt avvay him ſelf?
For he that ſhal be aſhamed of me and of my vvordes, him the Sonne of man ſhal be aſhamed of, vvhen he ſhal come in his maieſtie, and his fathers, and of the holy Angels.
And I ſay to you aſſuredly, There be ſome ſtanding here that ſhal not taſt death, til they ſee the kingdom of God.
<cr>[1]</cr><na>[2]</na> And it came to paſſe after theſe vvordes almoſt eight daies, and he tooke Peter and Iames and Iohn, and vvent into a mountaine to pray.

notes.text: The TRANSFIGVRATION.

verses.text: And vvhiles he prayed, the ſhape of his countenance vvas altered: and his raiment vvhite and gliſtering.
And behold tvvo men talked vvith him. And they vvere Moyſes and Elias,
appearing in maieſtie. And they told his deceaſe that he ſhould accompliſh in Hieruſalem.
But Peter and they that vvere vvith him, vvere heauie vvith ſleepe. And avvaking, they ſavv his maieſtie, and the tvvo men that ſtoode vvith him.

And it came to paſſe, vvhen they departed from him, Peter ſaid to <sc>IESVS</sc>, Maiſter, it is good for vs to be here: and let vs make three tabernacles, one for thee, and one for Moyſes, and one for Elias: not knovving vvhat he ſaid.
And as he ſpake theſe things, there came a cloud, and ouerſhadovved them: and they feared, vvhen they entered into the cloude.
<cr>[1]</cr> And a voice vvas made out of the cloude, ſaying, This is my beloued ſonne, heare him.
And vvhiles the voice vvas made, <sc>IESVS</sc> vvas found alone. And they held their peace, and told no man in thoſe daies any of theſe things vvhich they had ſeen.
<cr>[1]</cr> And it came to paſſe the day folovving, vvhen they came dovvne from the mountaine, there mette him a great multitude.
And behold a man of the multitude cried out, ſaying, Maiſter, I beſeeche thee, looke vpon my ſonne becauſe he is mine only one.
and loe, the ſpirit taketh him, and he ſodenly crieth, and he daſheth him, and teareth him that he fometh, and vvith much a doe departeth renting him.
And I deſired thy diſciples to caſt him out, and they could not.
And <sc>IESVS</sc> anſvvering ſaid, <na>[1]</na> O faithles and peruerſe generation, how long ſhal I be vvith you and ſuffer you? bring hither thy ſonne.

notes.text: Incredulitie hindereth the effect of Exorciſmes, and other miraculous power giuen to the Church.

verses.text: And vvhen he came to him, the deuil daſhed, and tore him. And <sc>IESVS</sc> rebuked the vncleane ſpirit, and healed the lad: and rendred him to his father.
And al vvere aſtonied at the might of God: and al merueiling at al things that he did, he ſaid to his diſciples,
Lay you in your hartes theſe vvordes, for it ſhal come to paſſe that the Sonne of man ſhal be deliuered into the hands of men.
But they did not know this vvord, and it vvas couered before them, that they perceiued it not. And they vvere afraid to aſke him of this vvord.
<cr>[1]</cr> And there entred <na>[2]</na> a cogitation into them, vvhich of them ſhould be greater.

notes.text: Deſire of preeminence is an humane infirmitie often euen among the good. Againſt which, Chriſt teacheth humility, but forbiddeth not Superiority.

verses.text: But <sc>IESVS</sc> ſeeing the cogitations of their hart, tooke a childe and ſet him by him,
and ſaid to them, Whoſoeuer receiueth this childe in my name, receiueth me: and vvhoſoeuer receiueth me, receiueth him that ſent me. For he that is the leſſer among you al, he is the greater.
<cr>[1]</cr> And Iohn anſvvering ſaid, Maiſter, vve ſavv a certaine man caſting out deuils in thy name, and vve prohibited him, becauſe he folovveth not vvith vs.
And <sc>IESVS</sc> ſaid to him, <na>[1]</na> Prohibit not. for he that is not againſt you, is for you.

notes.text: There be ſome that folow not Chriſt preciſely in life and doctrine, of whom vve may make our aduantage to the propagation of Chriſtes honour and religion, when they doe any thing for the aduancement thereof, of vvhat intention ſoeuer they doe it. Philip. 1, 15.

verses.text: And it came to paſſe, vvhiles the daies of his aſſumption vvere accompliſhing, and he fixed his face to goe into Hieruſalem.
And he ſent meſſengers before his face: and going they entred into a citie of the Samaritans to prepare for him.
And they receiued him not, becauſe his face vvas to goe to Hieruſalem.
And vvhen his diſciples Iames and Iohn had ſeen it, they ſaid, Lord vvilt thou vve ſay that fire come dovvne from heauen and conſume <na>[1]</na> <alt>`them</alt>'?

notes.text: `them as Elias alſo did?

verses.text: And turning, he rebuked them, ſaying, You knovv not of vvhat ſpirit you are.
The ſonne of man came not to deſtroy ſoules, but to ſaue. And they vvent into an other tovvne.
And it came to paſſe as they vvalked in the vvay, a certaine man ſaid to him, <cr>[1]</cr> I vvil folovv thee vvhitherſoeuer thou goeſt.
<sc>IESVS</sc> ſaid to him, <na>[1]</na> The foxes haue holes, and the foules of the aire neſtes: but the ſonne of man hath not where to repoſe his head.

notes.text: This man would haue folowed him for temporal commodities, and therfore was not ſuffered.

verses.text: But he ſaid to an other, Folow me. And he ſaid, Lord, permit me firſt to goe, and to burie my father.
And <sc>IESVS</sc> ſaid to him, Let the dead burie their dead: but goe thou, ſet forth the kingdom of God.
And an other ſaid, I vvil folovv thee Lord, but permit me firſt to take my leaue of them that are at home.
<sc>IESVS</sc> ſaid to him, No man putting his hand to the plough, and looking backe, is apt for the kingdom of God.

chapters.summary: His Twelue alſo now preaching euery where and working miracles. 6. Herod and al do wonder much. 10. After which, he taketh them and goeth into the vvilderneſſe: where he cureth and teacheth, feeding 5000 with fiue loaues. 18. Peter confeſſing him to be Chriſt, 21. he on the other ſide foretelleth his Paſſion, and that al muſt in time of perſecution folow him therein. 27. Wherevnto to encourage vs the more, 27. he giueth in his Transfiguration a ſight of the glorie, which is the reward of ſuffering. 37. The next day he caſteth out a diuel vvhich his Diſciples could not. 43. Whom amiddes theſe vvonders he forevvarneth againe of his ſcandalous Paſsion. 49. And to cure their ambition, he telleth them, that the moſt humble he eſteemeth moſt: 49. bidding them alſo, not to prohibit any that is not againſt them. 51. Yea and tovvard ſuch as be againſt them Schiſmatically, to ſhew mildnes for al that. 57. Of folowing him, three examples.

verses.text: <sc>AND</sc> <na>[1]</na> after this our Lord deſigned alſo other <na>[2]</na> ſeuentie tvvo: and he ſent them tvvo and tvvo before his face into euery citie and place vvhither him ſelf vvould come.

notes.text: The Goſpel upon S. Mark's day. April. 25. and S. Luke's Octob. 18.
As the twelue Apoſtles did repreſent the higher degree of the clergie, called Biſhops: ſo theſe Seuentie two beare the figure of the inferiour clergie, called Prieſts. Beda.

verses.text: And he ſaid to them, The harueſt truely is much: but the vvorkemen fevv. Deſire therfore the lord of the harueſt, that he ſend vvorkemen into his harueſt.
Goe: behold I ſend you as lambes among wolues.
Carie not purſe nor ſkrip, nor ſhoes: and ſalute no body by the vvay.
Into vvhatſoeuer houſe you enter, firſt ſay, Peace to this houſe.
and if the ſonne of peace be there, your peace ſhal reſt vpon him: but if not, it ſhal returne to you.
And in the ſame houſe tarie you, eating and drinking ſuch things as they haue. <cr>[1]</cr> For the vvorkeman is vvorthie of his hire. Remoue not from houſe to houſe.
And into vvhat citie ſoeuer you enter, and they receiue you, eate ſuch things as are ſet before you:
and cure the ſicke that are in it, and ſay to them, The kingdom of God is come nigh vpon you. ⊢
And into vvhatſoeuer citie you enter, and they receiue you not, going forth into the ſtreates thereof, ſay,
The duſt alſo of your citie that cleaueth to vs, vve doe vvipe of againſt you. yet this knovv ye that the kingdom of God is at hand.
I ſay to you, it ſhal be <na>[1]</na> more tolerable for Sodom in that day, then for that citie.

notes.text: Differences of paines and damnation in Hel according to the differences of demerites. Aug. li. 5. c. 5. cont. Iulian.

verses.text: VVo to thee Corozáim, vvo to thee Beth-ſaida: for if in Tyre and Sidon had been vvrought the miracles that haue beene vvrought in you, they had done penance ſitting <na>[1]</na> in ſacke cloth and aſhes long agoe.

notes.text: True penance not onely to lead a new life, but to puniſh the body by ſuch things as here be recorded, for the il life paſt.

verses.text: But it ſhal be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon in the iudgement, then for you.
And thou Capharnaum that art exalted vnto heauen: thou ſhalt be thruſt dovvne euen vnto hel.
<na>[1]</na><na>[2]</na> He that heareth you, heareth me: and he that deſpiſeth you, deſpiſeth me. And he that deſpiſeth me, deſpiſeth him that ſent me.

notes.text: The Goſpel for many Martyrs.
It is al one to deſpiſe Chriſt, and to deſpiſe his Prieſts and Miniſters in the the Catholike Church: to refuſe his doctrine, & theirs.

verses.text: And the Seuentie-tvvo returned vvith ioy, ſaying, Lord, the Deuils alſo are ſubiect to vs in thy name.
And he ſaid to them, I ſavv Satan as a lightening fal from heauen.
Behold, I haue giuen you povver to treade vpon ſerpents, and ſcorpions, and vpon al the povver of the enemie, and nothing ſhal hurt you.
But yet reioyce not in this, that the ſpirits are ſubiect vnto you: but reioyce in this, that your names are written in heauen. ⊢

In that very houre he reioyced in ſpirit, and ſaid, I confeſſe to thee O Father, Lord of heauen and earth, becauſe thou haſt hid theſe things from the wiſe and prudent, and haſt reuealed them to litle ones. Yea Father, for ſo hath it wel pleaſed thee.
Al things are deliuered to me of my father. And no man knovveth vvho the Sonne is, but the Father: and vvho the Father is, but the Sonne, and to vvhom the Sonne vvil reueale.
And turning to his Diſciples, he ſaid, Bleſſed are the eies that ſee the things that you ſee.
<na>[1]</na> For I ſay to you, that many Prophets and Kings deſired to ſee the things that you ſee, and ſaw them not: and to heare the things that you heare, and heard them not.

notes.text: The Goſpel vpon the 12 Sunday after Pentecoſt.

verses.text: And behold a certaine lavvyer ſtoode vp, tempting him and ſaying, Maiſter, by doing of what thing ſhal I poſſeſſe life euerlaſting?
But he ſaid to him, In the law vvhat is vvritten? hovv readeſt thou?
He anſvvering ſaid, [1] Thou ſhalt loue the Lord thy God vvith thy whole hart, and with thy whole ſoule, and with al thy ſtrength, and vvith al thy minde: and thy neighbour as thy ſelf. [2]
And he ſaid to him, Thou haſt anſvvered right, this doe and thou ſhalt liue.
But he deſirous to iuſtifie him ſelf, ſaid to <sc>IESVS</sc>, And vvho is my neighbour?
And <sc>IESVS</sc> taking it, ſaid, A certaine man vvent dovvne from Hieruſalem into Iericho, and fel among theeues, vvho alſo ſpoiled him, and giuing him vvoundes vvent avvay leauing him halfe-dead.
And it chaunced that a certaine Prieſt vvent dovvne the ſame vvay: and ſeeing him, paſſed by.
In like maner alſo a Leuite, vvhen he vvas neere the place, and ſavv him, paſſed by.
But a certaine Samaritane going his iourney, came neere him: and ſeeing him, was moued vvith mercie.
And going vnto him, bound his vvoundes, povvring in oile and vvine: and ſetting him vpon his ovvne beaſt, brought him into an inne, and tooke care of him.
And the next day he tooke forth two pence, and gaue to the hoſt, and ſaid, Haue care of him: and whatſoeuer thou ſhalt <na>[1]</na><na>[2]</na> ſupererogate, I at my returne vvil repay thee.

notes.text: S. Auguſtin ſaith that the Apoſtle (1.
